Lead story · Wayfinding · V&A East Storehouse · Dezeen · 13 Nov

A museum that signposts like an app

To make a London museum store feel welcoming to young visitors, studio Fieldwork Facility studied the apps Gen Z already uses and designed the signage like an operating system: onboarding, colour-coded zones and letters staff can rearrange.

The brief. V&A East Storehouse, designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro, opened the V&A's storage vault to the public, with about 250,000 art, craft and design objects. Studio founder Robin Howie says many people walk into museums with a feeling of "this isn't really for me". The wayfinding had to fix that.

Borrowed from apps. The team studied popular Gen Z apps such as TikTok. Visitors first meet "onboarding text", like opening an app for the first time. Three colours mark the zones: yellow for viewing galleries, green for the restoration labs and pink for the Study Centre, where anyone can order an object to see.

Signs you can reprogram. Recycled paper tiles, each with one letter like a Scrabble tile, sit in aluminium cases, so staff can change signs as objects move. For this, the studio commissioned Spiller Mono, a monospaced version of the V&A typeface, where every letter takes the same width, a nod to code and "building as software".

Built to change. Labels are a kit that clips onto crates, pallets and forklift shelving, with digital templates staff can edit themselves. Visitors can vote with coins at "expression points". Permanent icons such as toilets and lifts are painted on walls instead of vinyl. The project is shortlisted for graphic design of the year at the 2026 Dezeen Awards.

What this means for you

Your audience already knows a design language from the apps on their phone. Borrow its patterns (onboarding, colour tabs, simple icons) for print and space, not just screens. And design systems that the client's team can update without calling you: modular parts, editable templates and one rule for colour.

AI Desk

Anthropic · Claude Fable 5.2 · 15 Nov

An AI that paints stroke by stroke

Instead of diffusion, Claude Fable 5.2 writes Python code that drives a simulated paint engine with bristles, wet paint and canvas texture. One near-photo painting used about 700,000 strokes. In another test, a bird at sunrise took 111 strokes with no undo; the model painted over its own mistakes, like a human painter.

Adobe Firefly · Opinion · Creative Bloq · 15 Nov

Is "commercially safe" still safe?

Firefly was sold on licensed training data. Now models from OpenAI, Google, ByteDance and Kling sit inside it too, each with its own terms. Ian Dean argues a Firefly badge is not a Firefly guarantee, and asks Adobe to label every model's training data and let studios lock workspaces to Firefly-only models.

MiniMax · H3-Image · Kombitz · 14 Nov

Open 16-megapixel images in six steps

MiniMax released open weights for H3-Image, one model for creating and editing, making images of about 16 MP in six steps and taking up to 16 reference images. The full files are about 135 GB, and the licence excludes the US, EU, UK and South Korea, so read it before you build on it.

Prompt of the day · Test it, score it, then redesign it

The Press Day Spot Illustration

Happy National Press Day. Today's brief: a 3:2 editorial spot illustration for the opinion page of an invented newspaper, Samachar Setu, on the theme "Check before you share". Editorial art tests what AI finds hard: one clear metaphor, a strict palette, print texture and exact small text.

Score: 0 / 5

Student task: place your best result on a mock opinion page in Figma (A3, 6-column grid). Add a headline, a 2-line standfirst and a byline in the empty top third. Then crop the art to 1:1 for Instagram: does the metaphor still read at thumbnail size?

Version 1 · Any tool
A 3:2 editorial spot illustration for a newspaper opinion page, theme "Check before you share". On dark ink-black water, one small paper boat folded from newsprint sails towards the right. On the left, a lighthouse made of one upright fountain pen; exactly 3 straight light rays come from its nib and light the boat. The sail shows "सच" in red. Only three colours: ink black, newsprint cream, one red. Visible halftone dot texture like old print. Keep the top third empty. No people, hands, logos or other text.

Why it works: one metaphor, counted elements and a fixed palette make the result easy to score.

Version 2 · Midjourney V8
editorial spot illustration, single paper boat folded from newsprint on dark ink water, lighthouse made of an upright fountain pen, three straight light beams from the nib, halftone dot print texture, three colour risograph, ink black, newsprint cream and red, empty top third, minimal, newspaper opinion page --ar 3:2 --style raw --stylize 120 --no text, letters, people, hands, logos

V8 tip: leave the sail blank here and add सच yourself in Figma; check that V8 does not add extra boats or rays.

Version 3 · Nano Banana
Step 1: Make the illustration from Version 1 but leave the sail blank. Keep the top third empty. No people, no hands.
Step 2 (same chat): Keep everything exactly the same. Write "सच" on the sail in red, hand-lettered, following the sail's curve. Do not change the boat, the pen, the 3 rays or the palette.

What you are testing: whether step 2 adds Devanagari on a curved surface without redrawing the scene.

Version 4 · ChatGPT
Create a 3:2 editorial spot illustration for the opinion page of the newspaper Samachar Setu.
Layout:
1. Top third: empty newsprint cream, for a headline
2. Background: dark ink-black water across the bottom two thirds
3. Left: one upright fountain pen as a lighthouse
4. From the nib: exactly 3 straight light rays
5. Right: one paper boat folded from newsprint
6. Sail: "सच" in red, the only text
Style: three colours only (ink black, cream, red), halftone dots, flat print look. No people, hands or logos.

Tip: if the rays are wrong, reply "fix only the light rays: exactly 3; keep everything else the same".

Graphic Design

Pixel art · Klas Benjaminsson · 15 Nov

A new poster on a 30-year-old computer

Swedish pixel artist Klas Benjaminsson made his poster Beyond the Screen on an original Amiga 1200: just 640 × 512 pixels and 32 colours, sketched in pencil, then painted in Deluxe Paint 4. He calls those limits a "sweet spot": tight enough to push against, generous enough to make something great.

Material · Arudeko · Dezeen · 14 Nov

Paper woven with waste wool

Mexican studio Arudeko weaves leftover dyed wool from Oaxaca rug workshops with strips of recycled paper made by local papermakers. The result, Bianni, is translucent and flexible, used for lampshades and room dividers, and the wool adds fire resistance. No additives, just natural fibres.

Poster · Lego · Creative Bloq · 15 Nov

A film poster rebuilt in bricks

Lego's anniversary set recreates the classic A New Hope poster in 3,209 pieces, sized to hang as wall art. Designer Steven Howard says the logo was the hardest part, so the title is slightly bigger than on the original, 32 studs wide. It costs $299 and arrives on 4 January. Type always fights the grid.

UI / UX

Apple · Smart glasses · MacRumors · 15 Nov

Apple's glasses will have no screen

According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple plans to show its first smart glasses at WWDC in June 2027. They will have cameras but no display: people will talk to Siri, which can read signs, translate and give directions. Apps stay on the iPhone, so designers must expose app actions to Siri, from ordering coffee to booking a table.

Tesla · Cybercab · Creative Bloq · 15 Nov

A car that stops working when you cancel

Tesla's Cybercab costs $29,990, plus a $299-a-month Autonomy Subscription. It has no manual controls, so cancelling does not downgrade it: it leaves an expensive object in your driveway. Even Elon Musk called the fee "too high". When a subscription is the only way a product works, the exit is part of the design.

WhatsApp · iOS beta 26.45.10.70 · 16 Nov

Glass reaches the last screens

WhatsApp is adding Apple's Liquid Glass look to two more iOS screens for some beta testers: the action buttons in chat info (call, status, add, search) and the drawing editor's toolbar. A design system rollout is only finished when the last odd screen matches.

Student Corner

Careers · Adgully Young Guns · 14 Nov

From pastry kitchen to brand studio

Art director Ayushi Jain trained in kitchens before design. She says cooking taught her discipline and showing up daily, and that both crafts combine many parts into one dish. Landor taught her systems-led thinking; India-based boutique studio Pollinate Labs gave her room to obsess over craft and grow into strategy.

Jobs · Reserve Bank of Australia · The Decoder · 15 Nov

AI is hitting entry-level jobs first

A Reserve Bank of Australia study finds AI has barely removed jobs overall, but job ads fell most in highly exposed fields, and young workers there are doing worse. It does not prove AI is the cause. For students, the message is clear: show judgement and craft that a tool cannot copy.

Design psychology term of the day

Jakob's law

People spend most of their time on other products, so they expect yours to work the same way. Familiar patterns let them skip learning and get to the content. It is why a museum can borrow app onboarding and colour tabs.

Try it: list the three apps your audience uses most. Borrow one pattern they already know, and break convention only where it adds real value.

Indian Design Watch

Design in India
Identity · Khelo India Youth Games · 15 Nov

A logo built from Telangana's skyline

The 8th Khelo India Youth Games logo (11–22 Dec) packs eight elements: Gandhi Tower, Kakatiya Kala Thoranam, the Hussain Sagar Buddha, the Tangedu flower and seven sports silhouettes inside a ribbon. Mascot: Neelamani, a blue bird.

Play design · Aga Khan Foundation · 14 Nov

A play corner in every home

In 400+ homes in Bihar, East Delhi, UP and Telangana, families set up a "Khel Kona": toys made from scrap fabric, cardboard puzzles and coloured corn-cob garlands, matched to ages 0–3 and 3–6. Low cost, high care.

New campaigns
SBI · Dora Digs · 13 Nov

"Ghar Se Dur, Ghar Wali Diwali"

Most Diwali ads celebrate going home. This film, written by Ankur Jain and directed by Akshay Shah, follows people who stay back for work and find family in small kindnesses. Lesson: flip the category cliché.

Rampur Indian Single Malt · 13 Nov

"43° | 2° – Born in Nature's Frequency"

A new platform built on two numbers: 43°C summers and 2°C winters at the Himalayan-foothill distillery. Read together they make "432", now the brand's numerical signature. A brand truth turned into a graphic device.

Agency news & awards
CII Design Excellence Awards · 12 Nov

Ahmedabad studio wins product design Gold

iMAC Design & Engineering Services won Gold in Product Design at the 16th CII Design Excellence Awards for its engineering on Mecha Comet, a modular Linux handheld by Mecha Systems: module interfaces, tolerances and heat, from concept to prototype.

Havas Media Network India · 16 Nov

Havas wins Milky Mist's Capella

Havas Media Network India won the integrated mandate for Capella, Milky Mist's luxury chocolate line. Havas Media India handles media and performance; PivotRoots, led by co-founder and CCO Hetal Khalsa, leads creative and content.
